preconditions: Distinguish the read-only prompt hook from installation or policy-authoring operations that write project files.
Treat the supplied project path as task-scoped input; policy and agent-instruction writes require authorization for that project.
Prompt text, local skill metadata and injected guidance can enter the active model context; apply the task's disclosure rules before using the hook.
A prefer-local recommendation does not prove that a local model, MCP tool, terminal wrapper or target harness is installed, healthy or appropriate for the current task.

expected_effects.effect: Read a bounded submitted prompt and project path, assess supported work locally, and selectively emit advisory preflight context to stdout.
expected_effects.scope: Accepted prompt/event text, local Botte/project skill metadata and the current Claude Code hook context receiving stdout; no model, network request or tool execution occurs in this path.
expected_effects.basis: hook.py accepts bounded JSON events or plain prompts and calls assessment.assess_task. Unsupported, trivial, negated, malformed or oversized work emits no context; a detected mixed workflow may emit an abstention notice. Supported intents receive bounded specific guidance, with optional filtered skill-name hints except for GitHub research. Hook errors leave the prompt unblocked.
expected_effects.impact: Adds task-specific advice and possible skill names to the receiving model context. It consumes local CPU/I/O and host context, while availability, authorization, timing and savings remain unverified.
expected_effects.verification: Use fixed prompt/cwd fixtures for supported calculations, duplicates, local links and GitHub work, mixed/negated work, malformed events and failures. Assert specific evidence guidance survives, output bounds and exit zero hold, and no project writes, process launch or network calls occur.

expected_effects.effect: Create a default .botte/policy.md when policy.write_default is called and no policy exists, or replace it only when overwrite is explicitly requested.
expected_effects.scope: The selected project's .botte directory and policy file.
expected_effects.basis: policy.write_default checks existence, creates parent directories and writes DEFAULT_POLICY; the default overwrite flag is false.
expected_effects.impact: Persists shared routing, hygiene and budget guidance for later agents/developers; an incorrect project path or deliberate overwrite can replace intended project policy.
expected_effects.verification: Run against a temporary project, verify first-write and no-op repeat behavior, then separately verify explicit overwrite behavior on controlled content.

expected_effects.effect: Append a pointer to .botte/policy.md to the first existing AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md that lacks the pointer when ensure_agents_pointer is called.
expected_effects.scope: One selected project instruction file and every later agent session that consumes it.
expected_effects.basis: policy.ensure_agents_pointer checks AGENTS.md then CLAUDE.md, skips files already containing the policy path, and appends AGENTS_POINTER to the first writable match.
expected_effects.impact: Makes the shared policy persistent across future sessions; it modifies an instruction source and can change later routing behavior even though the current hook itself is fail-open.
expected_effects.verification: Use temporary AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md fixtures to verify append-once semantics, file precedence, missing-file behavior and unchanged content on retry.

downstream_effects.effect: Future agents may choose local tools, improve prompts or run checkups because injected or committed policy guidance remains in their context.
downstream_effects.scope: Later task routing, model/tool selection, token use and project maintenance decisions.
downstream_effects.basis: The existing Claude Code hook emits guidance selectively; separately committed policy and instruction pointers persist. The consuming host must load them and choose actions; no instruction is installed into an unsupported host by this hook.
downstream_effects.impact: Guidance may influence routing, but lexical matches and repeated instructions do not establish suitability, tool availability, fewer tokens or better results. Stale or over-broad guidance can bias later choices.
downstream_effects.verification: Compare a fixed set of representative tasks with and without the preflight context; record selected routes, task quality, total cost and abstentions rather than assuming the policy helped.

downstream_effects.effect: A project policy edit can propagate through version control, shared worktrees or other automation that reads AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md.
downstream_effects.scope: Collaborators and agents consuming the modified project files after the write is shared.
downstream_effects.basis: The files are ordinary persistent project files; propagation depends on the repository and synchronization workflow outside this skill.
downstream_effects.impact: A mistaken rule can outlive the initiating session; a correct rule can prevent opt-in drift across agents.
downstream_effects.verification: Review the exact diff and repository state before sharing; confirm downstream consumers read the intended project/version rather than a stale copy.

reversibility.strategy: The prompt hook is read-only with respect to project files. Revert policy or instruction-file changes with the project's normal version/file rollback after inspecting the exact diff; disable or remove hook wiring separately when applicable.
residual_effects: Guidance already injected into the current model context cannot be retroactively unseen.
Copied, committed or synchronized policy text may persist in histories or downstream worktrees after a local revert.

retry.check_before_retry: Check whether the hook already produced context for the current turn and inspect existing .botte/policy.md plus AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md before repeating any write. Do not use overwrite merely to refresh a file without reviewing semantic drift.
retry.stop_condition: Stop when the desired policy/pointer already exists, when project scope is uncertain, or when routing guidance conflicts with a higher-priority task requirement or unavailable local capability.

required_scope: The hook needs read access to prompt input and local skill metadata. Writing policy or agent-instruction pointers needs explicit task authority for the selected project files; neither the declaration nor a hook installation grants that authority.

analysis.summary: Preflight separates bounded local assessment and selective context emission from persistent policy-authoring operations. Its outputs are advisory; source freshness, task scope and actual host behavior matter, and no measured saving or automatic local execution follows from a lexical proposal.
uncertainties: The declaration does not bind bootstrap/deployer code that may wire the hook into harness settings, so installation-side writes must be assessed separately.
The actual local model/tool availability and quality are runtime properties not verified by this skill.
The hook intentionally swallows exceptions; absence of injected context can therefore look like ordinary success unless the caller verifies stdout when that distinction matters.

Skill-finder ranking is an imported dependency outside these source hashes. Matching metadata does not validate a capability, and this Claude Code hook does not provide a Codex/Work-cloud lifecycle adapter.

reuse.target: Adapt the pre-prompt policy injector to another agent harness or repository without transferring Botte-specific routing assumptions blindly.
reuse.rationale: The hook is standalone stdin/stdout logic and the persistent policy is an ordinary project file, so the mechanism is portable even when tool names and routing economics differ.
adaptations: Map the target harness's pre-prompt hook contract and failure semantics explicitly.
Replace Botte-specific tool names, token budgets and project-instruction conventions with target-validated equivalents.
Measure whether the target's local route preserves task quality before promoting repeated routing guidance.
reuse.validation: Replay representative cheap and reasoning-heavy prompts in the target harness, including unavailable-local-tool and hook-error fixtures; compare route, quality, cost and whether user prompts remain unblocked.
